method: Closed-form Young-Laplace liquid-entry pressure for a cylindrical pore plus a Bosanquet (bulk+Knudsen) steady-diffusion O2 budget. No fitted parameters.
field_pressure_note: hand-set scenarios, not site data; the upper bound is submersion_50mm, not the wind-driven rain; droplet impact (water hammer) is not modelled

o2_budget.j_max_provenance: lib.constants J_MAX_25C is the ANODE pair's literature current density; used here as the cathode demand only because the cell is in series

verdict: 1. The specified pore window holds 10-74 m of water head against hand-set field loads of 10-489 Pa. Against THOSE loads the nominal pore is not the limit; what remains — a web/seam defect, and loss of hydrophobicity — this formula does not compute. 2. The prescribed 30 cm column only fails pores wider than 34 um, so it is a gross-defect detector. Keep it as such, and verify the pore spec with the bubble-point rig the sterilisation QC already needs (100 kPa for the widest spec pore). 3. The §5.3 prose bound 'no pores > 15 um' is NOT an arithmetic error: it is this same inversion at 120 deg (14.87 um). What is missing is the slice — the §5.3 TABLE guarantees only 110 deg, which demands <= 10.2 um. State theta with the number or neither means anything. 4. The design's real exposure is theta, not pore size: the worst hand-set field load breaks through only once the contact angle falls to 90.02-90.10 deg. That is the acceptance number the 12-week rain/dew test has been missing. 5. O2 transport exceeds the cathode's peak demand by 8,627x at the worst pore in the whole 0.02-15 um range, so if the cathode is O2-limited the bottleneck is the catalytic layer, not the GDL. (The demand uses the anode pair's literature current density — legitimate only because the cell is in series.)
ceilings: Nominal cylindrical pores — a real web is a distribution with a tail, and the largest as-made pore governs; no Cassie/Wenzel roughness correction; contact angle is the spec claim, not our measurement; the O2 half assumes a dry, open membrane (wetting, condensation and dust blinding are the real failure mode and are not modelled).
